policy: Dedicated video-hallucination benchmarks only. Named dedicated datasets may be scoped separately; generic tasks or a hallucination metric alone do not qualify.

records.protocol: Native Reference, Shot, and Event tracks; structural checks and localized semantic precision/recall.
records.rationale: The core target is comprehensive audio-visual caption evaluation. Hallucination-sensitive precision is real, but does not make the whole benchmark a dedicated video-hallucination test. Removed under the explicitly approved strict policy.

original_entry.title: OmniCapBench: A Deep-Structured Evaluation Framework for Fine-Grained Audio-Visual Captioning
original_entry.name: OmniCapBench
original_entry.description: Evaluates structured audio-visual captions using grounded precision, identity consistency, and event-shot association to expose hallucinated descriptions and cross-modal attribution errors.

records.protocol: Adversarial action QA, temporal sorting, and scene-transition classification/description; paired accuracy and scene scores.
records.rationale: The benchmark is explicitly constructed to diagnose action, temporal-sequence, and scene-transition hallucinations in video responses.

original_entry.title: VidHalluc: Evaluating Temporal Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models for Video Understanding
original_entry.name: VidHalluc
original_entry.description: Evaluates hallucinations about actions, temporal order, and scene transitions through video questions, caption generation, and event sorting.

records.protocol: Hallucination-triggering object, scene, and event questions; judged answer accuracy and cross-variant bias.
records.rationale: Video hallucination is the benchmark objective and determines its causes-by-aspects-by-question-format design.

original_entry.title: Exploring Hallucination of Large Multimodal Models in Video Understanding: Benchmark, Analysis and Mitigation
original_entry.name: HAVEN
original_entry.description: Diagnoses video hallucinations by crossing hallucination causes, object-scene-event aspects, and question formats to expose distinct failures in video understanding.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Motion Hallucination Benchmark and Motion Hallucination Evaluation (AAAI PDF pp. 4403-4404)
records.protocol: Original, antonym, and incomplete-action videos; paired binary accuracy, Yes/No bias, and action-classification F1.
records.rationale: Directly tests whether static appearance induces claims about absent or different motions.

original_entry.title: MHBench: Demystifying Motion Hallucination in VideoLLMs
original_entry.name: MHBench
original_entry.description: Tests motion hallucinations using original actions, actions with reversed meanings, and incomplete actions that challenge static visual cues.

records.protocol: KPM-HA contains 215 manually annotated videos; GPT-Hall and Mo-Hall assess fabricated actions, order, and direction.
records.rationale: Retain the explicitly named hallucination evaluation set KPM-HA, not the broader KPM-Cap/KPM-QA suite.

original_entry.title: KPM-Bench: A Kinematic Parsing Motion Benchmark for Fine-grained Motion-centric Video Understanding
original_entry.name: KPM-Bench
original_entry.description: Evaluates fine-grained limb motion through video captioning and question answering, using kinematic parsing to assess motion descriptions.

records.protocol: ArgusBench video captions are checked by sentence entailment and temporal alignment; ArgusCost-H is paired with omission cost.
records.rationale: Measuring unsupported free-form video claims is the central objective; omission scoring prevents empty captions from appearing optimal. ArgusBench is the dataset within ARGUS.

original_entry.title: ARGUS: Hallucination and Omission Evaluation in Video-LLMs
original_entry.name: ARGUS
original_entry.description: Measures both fabricated content and missing information in free-form video captions against human-written reference descriptions.

records.protocol: Paired videos and adversarial questions assess directional, attributional, and temporal motion errors.
records.rationale: Explicitly evaluates kinematic hallucinations rather than generic action-recognition accuracy.

original_entry.title: MotionHalluc: Diagnosing Kinematic Hallucinations in Fine-Grained Motion Reasoning
original_entry.name: MotionHalluc
original_entry.description: Diagnoses fine-grained motion hallucinations involving direction, attribution, and temporal kinematics, separating distinct failures in interpreting physical movement.

records.protocol: Debiased positive/negative accuracy, question-pair accuracy, consistency, and hallucinated-outcome rate on truncated clips.
records.rationale: Targets co-occurrence, sequential-inference, and similarity-induced motion hallucinations; consistency alone is not its hallucination outcome.

original_entry.title: MoHallBench: A Benchmark for Motion Hallucination in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: MoHallBench
original_entry.description: Probes motion hallucinations caused by prior knowledge, sequential inference, and visual similarity through several question formats.

records.protocol: Basic/hallucinated VideoQA pairs; both answers must be correct, with Yes-bias diagnostics.
records.rationale: Dedicated intrinsic and extrinsic video hallucination evaluation, including unsupported facts that are true outside the video.

original_entry.title: VideoHallucer: Evaluating Intrinsic and Extrinsic Hallucinations in Large Video-Language Models
original_entry.name: VideoHallucer
original_entry.description: Uses adversarial question pairs to distinguish hallucinations about visible objects and temporal relations from unsupported external information.

records.protocol: Six streaming-video capabilities and 16 subtasks, including Temporal Hallucination Verification (THV).
records.rationale: The overall benchmark targets online perception, memory, and reasoning. THV is one task, not a separately introduced hallucination benchmark. VideoChat-Online remains a separate method entry.

original_entry.title: Online Video Understanding: OVBench and VideoChat-Online
original_entry.name: OVBench
original_entry.description: Evaluates streaming-video question answering across online perception, memory, and reasoning tasks; its scope extends beyond hallucination-specific evaluation.

records.protocol: Select or rank captions with graded temporal hallucinations; MCQA accuracy and adapted NDCG.
records.rationale: The construction and ranking target explicitly measure nuanced video hallucination severity.

original_entry.title: VidHal: Benchmarking Temporal Hallucinations in Vision LLMs
original_entry.name: VidHal
original_entry.description: Evaluates temporal hallucinations by asking models to distinguish and rank video captions with different degrees of factual distortion.

records.protocol: Object/action precision, recall, and F1 against dense reference captions in Vript-HAL.
records.rationale: Vript-HAL is a named dedicated hallucination benchmark. Vript corpus, Vript-RR, Vript-ERO, and Vriptor have broader purposes.

original_entry.title: Vript: A Video Is Worth Thousands of Words
original_entry.name: Vript
original_entry.description: Provides dense video descriptions and Vript-Hard evaluations targeting hallucinated captions, information retrieval, and temporal ordering of video events.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Section 4: Hallucination Evaluation (ACL PDF p. 28466)
records.protocol: Hallucination-inducing egocentric visual/audio questions; binary matching and judged unsupported-premise/factual correctness.
records.rationale: Designed specifically to elicit and evaluate hallucinations in egocentric video understanding.

original_entry.title: EGOILLUSION: Benchmarking Hallucinations in Egocentric Video Understanding
original_entry.name: EGOILLUSION
original_entry.description: Tests hallucinations in first-person videos through human-annotated open and closed questions about visual and auditory evidence.

records.protocol: Target/trap questions on settings, character features, and subject-action binding; accuracy and response-balance metrics.
records.rationale: The primary diagnostic is video hallucination under progressively finer entity and action distinctions.

original_entry.title: MESH -- Understanding Videos Like Human: Measuring Hallucinations in Large Video Models
original_entry.name: MESH
original_entry.description: Uses hierarchical questions and plausible distractors to expose hallucinations about objects, attributes, and subject-action relations across video segments.

records.protocol: Ten temporal-object-consistency dimensions; exact-match scores and HDA on nonexistent-object/event variants.
records.rationale: HDA genuinely tests hallucination, but it is an auxiliary diagnostic within an object-consistency benchmark. The whole TOC-Bench does not meet the strict core-target criterion.

original_entry.title: TOC-Bench: A Temporal Object Consistency Benchmark for Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: TOC-Bench
original_entry.description: Tests object identity, state, and continuity with trajectory-grounded questions designed to require temporally ordered visual evidence.

records.protocol: Object-centric target/sub-question QA; Faithful Accuracy requires every prerequisite and final answer to be correct.
records.rationale: The core task is spatio-temporal monitoring and supported reasoning. Hallucination is a motivation and error category, but the benchmark is not dedicated to identifying unsupported claims. This is a conservative scope exclusion, not a claim of irrelevance; the trajectory-reasoning method is unchanged.

original_entry.title: STRAND: Benchmarking and Improving Object-Centric Spatio-Temporal Monitoring in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: STRAND
original_entry.description: Evaluates object-state changes, identity persistence, and relational reasoning, requiring answers to satisfy jointly grounded spatiotemporal prerequisites.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Final Benchmark and Evaluation Metrics: Accuracy and SAH Ratio
records.protocol: Ground-truth, in-video hallucination, and out-of-video hallucination questions; paired accuracy and SAH ratio.
records.rationale: Specifically diagnoses semantic misattribution across events in long videos; SAH ratio is a proxy based on accuracy differences.

original_entry.title: ELV-Halluc: Benchmarking Semantic Aggregation Hallucinations in Long Video Understanding
original_entry.name: ELV-Halluc
original_entry.description: Tests hallucinations from semantic aggregation in long videos, where models can incorrectly combine information across separate video segments.

records.protocol: Controlled and natural distractor segments; bag-of-events false-association rates with Yes/No-bias controls.
records.rationale: The central measured failure is hallucinating interactions between subjects and events from disjoint video segments.

original_entry.title: Pop-Up Distractions Reveal Bag-of-Events Behavior in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: DistractionBench
original_entry.description: Inserts advertising distractors into long videos to test whether models conflate subjects and events from unrelated segments.

records.protocol: Agent-centric gameplay QA across perception, temporal reasoning, and multi-POV understanding; distractor-conditioned error rates.
records.rationale: The benchmark primarily tests embodied perception and reasoning. Structured hallucination distractors enable error analysis but do not make the whole collection a dedicated hallucination benchmark. Restored to its original category under the owner's community-contribution preservation instruction; the earlier removal is superseded, not the scientific scope assessment. Originally accepted through PR #2 by wangyz1999.

original_entry.title: GameplayQA: A Benchmarking Framework for Decision-Dense POV-Synced Multi-Video Understanding of 3D Virtual Agents
original_entry.name: GameplayQA
original_entry.description: Uses synchronized multiplayer gameplay views and structured distractors to test agent identity, role attribution, and grounded reasoning.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 2 and 3: Answer Evaluation; Appendix F
records.protocol: QA about synthetic-video abnormalities, physics, commonsense, alignment, and consistency; judged answer correctness.
records.rationale: Under the strict rule, the core target is out-of-distribution visual reasoning and anomaly recognition, not a dedicated unsupported-claim evaluation. Appendix F also includes language-only commonsense questions. Prior-driven hallucinations are discussed, so this is a conservative scope exclusion, not a denial of relevance. VideoHallu-GRPO is unchanged.

original_entry.title: VideoHallu: Evaluating and Mitigating Multi-modal Hallucinations on Synthetic Video Understanding
original_entry.name: VideoHallu
original_entry.description: Tests prior-driven hallucinations using synthetic videos that violate physical or logical expectations, challenging models to follow observed evidence.

records.protocol: ActivityNet-Fact and YouCook2-Fact annotate paragraph, sentence, and word factual errors; metrics are compared with human judgments.
records.rationale: These are dedicated video-caption factuality datasets. FactVC is the associated learned metric, not the benchmark name; image-only experiments are outside this entry.

original_entry.title: Models See Hallucinations: Evaluating the Factuality in Video Captioning
original_entry.name: FactVC
original_entry.description: Studies factual errors in video captions and introduces a weakly supervised factuality metric with human-annotated evaluation data.

records.protocol: Limb-caption action/posture checklists and temporal coverage; GPA, weighted hallucination rate, and temporal-sequence accuracy.
records.rationale: The primary objective is comprehensive limb-motion caption fidelity and coverage. GPA/WHR explicitly penalize fabricated actions, but the whole benchmark is broader than the approved dedicated-hallucination scope. GM-DPO is unchanged.

original_entry.title: Beyond Binary Preferences: Graded Preference Optimization for Limb-Motion Captioning
original_entry.name: FlexBench
original_entry.description: Evaluates person-specific limb-motion captions across shots, distinguishing omissions from fabricated or incorrect actions through graded physical alignment.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; EventHallusion Benchmark: Evaluation Protocol
records.protocol: Misleading-event binary QA and open descriptions of infrequent events; answer correctness is scored against grounded references.
records.rationale: Dedicated to event hallucinations caused by language priors and spurious visual-event correlations.

original_entry.title: EventHallusion: Diagnosing Event Hallucinations in Video LLMs
original_entry.name: EventHallusion
original_entry.description: Diagnoses event hallucinations driven by language priors and visual biases, testing whether answers reflect events actually present in videos.

records.protocol: Inserted-event videos; caption/event hallucination and omission rates plus existence, temporal, and fabricated-narrative QA.
records.rationale: Narrative-prior-induced hallucination and omission are the benchmark targets, not incidental analyses of general caption quality.

original_entry.title: NOAH: Benchmarking Narrative Prior driven Hallucination and Omission in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: NOAH
original_entry.description: Inserts unrelated clips into videos to measure narrative-prior hallucinations and omissions through captioning and question-answering tasks.

records.protocol: Twelve road-event QA tasks; GPT answer scores and temporal-grounding mAP, with incompatible/adversarial question tasks.
records.rationale: The hallucination tests are genuine but subordinate to general road-event understanding. The broad RoadSocial benchmark is excluded under the strict policy.

original_entry.title: RoadSocial: A Diverse VideoQA Dataset and Benchmark for Road Event Understanding from Social Video Narratives
original_entry.name: RoadSocial
original_entry.description: Provides diverse social-media road videos and question-answer pairs for evaluating road-event understanding across viewpoints and geographic settings.

records.protocol: Scene-matched video/question quadruples require rejecting three false hypotheses; QuadAcc and negative-hallucination diagnostics.
records.rationale: Unsupported traffic-event assertions and counterfactual rejection are central to construction and scoring, rather than an optional general VideoQA analysis. NegHall is conditional on failed quadruples, not a corpus-wide hallucination rate.

original_entry.title: CCTVBench: Contrastive Consistency Traffic VideoQA Benchmark for Multimodal LLMs
original_entry.name: CCTVBench
original_entry.description: Tests consistent traffic-hazard judgments using real accident videos paired with counterfactual counterparts that alter the evidence for an accident.

records.protocol: Sentence-wise support labels for dense video captions; precision, recall, and F1 treat incorrect sentences as the detection target.
records.rationale: Despite a broad title, its actual benchmark task is detecting unsupported video-caption events.

original_entry.title: VidOmni-Bench: A Benchmark for Fine-Grained Video Understanding via Spatio-Temporal Event Verification across Complexity and Duration
original_entry.name: VidOmni-Bench
original_entry.description: Tests whether models can verify individual events in dense video captions, using human-checked incorrect descriptions as hard negatives.

records.protocol: Faithfulness/factuality QA with controlled video perturbations; base accuracy, Resist Rate, and Temporal Sensitivity Score.
records.rationale: Hallucination diagnosis is explicit and central. World-knowledge factuality is distinct from video faithfulness; TSS measures response change, not correctness after perturbation.

original_entry.title: INFACT: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Induced Faithfulness and Factuality Hallucinations in Video-LLMs
original_entry.name: INFACT
original_entry.description: Separates faithfulness from factuality errors in video answers and probes robustness to degraded visuals, corrupted evidence, and temporal interventions.

records.protocol: Isolated/compositional hallucination QA with adversarial options; accuracy, Yes/No accuracy, and macro precision/recall/F1.
records.rationale: Designed to test unsupported claims involving interacting video entities, actions, temporal relations, and camera factors.

original_entry.title: Learning to Decode Against Compositional Hallucination in Video Multimodal Large Language Models
original_entry.name: OmniVCHall
original_entry.description: Benchmarks isolated and compositional hallucinations across spatial and temporal dimensions, probing failures involving multiple interacting types of video evidence.

records.protocol: Reliability scores on SoccerChat outputs; ROC-AUC against LLM-judged hallucination labels.
records.rationale: VideoHEDGE is a hallucination-detection framework, not a newly introduced benchmark. Retain it under evaluation analyses as a detection study; do not imply it corrects generated answers.

original_entry.title: VideoHEDGE: Entropy-Based Hallucination Detection for Video-VLMs via Semantic Clustering and Spatiotemporal Perturbations
original_entry.name: VideoHEDGE
original_entry.description: Estimates answer reliability by clustering responses to clean and perturbed videos and measuring semantic uncertainty across those responses.

records.protocol: YouCook3-Fact and CraftBench-Fact provide role-annotated positive/negative facts; video-grounded verification separates hallucination, salience, and omission.
records.rationale: Retain the dedicated factuality datasets, not DualFact as a dataset name. Only video-grounded verification supports video hallucination judgments; textual verification can overcount them.

original_entry.title: DualFact+: A Multimodal Fact Verification Framework for Procedural Video Understanding
original_entry.name: DualFact
original_entry.description: Evaluates procedural-caption factuality at conceptual and grounded argument levels, using either textual references or direct video evidence.

records.protocol: Gaslighting changes an initially correct video answer into an incorrect one; conditional Sycophancy Rate and accuracy change.
records.rationale: The benchmark specifically probes conversationally induced, visually unsupported answers. Its operational outcome is answer reversal, not a separately quantified rate of fabricated explanatory details.

original_entry.title: Spatiotemporal Sycophancy: Negation-Based Gaslighting in Video Large Language Models
original_entry.name: GasVideo-1000
original_entry.description: Tests whether misleading conversational feedback causes video models to abandon correct judgments and invent unsupported spatiotemporal explanations.

records.protocol: Contradictory, congruent, and absent text overlays; Hallucination Resistance Rate on visually grounded questions.
records.rationale: Text-overlay-induced hallucination is the named failure mode and benchmark design target.

original_entry.title: When Text Hijacks Vision: Benchmarking and Mitigating Text Overlay-Induced Hallucination in Vision Language Models
original_entry.name: VisualTextTrap
original_entry.description: Tests whether misleading text overlays cause video models to contradict visual evidence when answering questions about the depicted content.

records.protocol: Background-controlled adversarial video pairs; question/video-pair accuracy, weighted accuracy, bias, and MCQ F1.
records.rationale: Explicitly diagnoses foreground-semantic hallucinations under controlled video differences, not video-generation quality.

original_entry.title: No Place to Hide: Benchmarking Video Hallucination with Background-Controlled Pairs
original_entry.name: VidPair-Halluc
original_entry.description: Uses adversarial video pairs with similar backgrounds but different foreground events to isolate spatial and temporal hallucinations.

records.protocol: VHD has visible, prior-conflicting, and hidden-evidence conditions; unanimous wrong-answer and conditional-consensus error rates.
records.rationale: The named diagnostic dataset directly targets shared confident video hallucinations. It is a development set, not the paper's independent held-out reliability-transfer test.

original_entry.title: Target-Checked Reliability Score Refinement for Video Question Answering
original_entry.name: VHD
original_entry.description: Provides controlled video-question examples of confident but incorrect answers for diagnosing hallucinations and evaluating the reliability of confidence estimates.

records.protocol: Detector decisions on factual/counterfactual video answers; factual, counterfactual, and joint Overall accuracy.
records.rationale: The central task is evaluating video hallucination detectors, distinct from measuring hallucination generation by answering models.

original_entry.title: Can We Trust Video Hallucination Detectors? VidHalLoc for Evaluating the Evaluators
original_entry.name: VidHalLoc
original_entry.description: Compares hallucination detectors on adversarial video questions and captions, with a shared protocol spanning ontology and dynamic errors.

records.protocol: Audio-driven video and video-driven audio hallucination tasks, matching, and captioning; binary metrics and caption assessment.
records.rationale: Cross-modal hallucination in audio-visual videos is the benchmark's explicit core objective. Matching and captioning support that analysis, but ordinary caption metrics are not hallucination rates.

original_entry.title: AVHBench: A Cross-Modal Hallucination Benchmark for Audio-Visual Large Language Models
original_entry.name: AVHBench
original_entry.description: Evaluates audio-visual hallucinations, cross-modal matching, and reasoning through tasks that distinguish auditory evidence from visible video content.

records.protocol: Video/video-audio object/event presence probes; Perception Accuracy and Hallucination Resistance for absent items.
records.rationale: A dedicated multimodal hallucination benchmark with actual video inputs. Limit this entry to video and audio-visual conditions, not audio-only evaluation.

original_entry.title: The Curse of Multi-Modalities: Evaluating Hallucinations of Large Multimodal Models across Language, Visual, and Audio
original_entry.name: CMM
original_entry.description: Investigates how unimodal priors and misleading correlations between language, vision, and audio cause multimodal hallucinations.

records.protocol: Sound-focused questions on egocentric videos, including absent sounds; LLM-judged correctness checked against human judgments.
records.rationale: Directly evaluates visually induced hallucinated sounds in video+audio understanding, not standalone audio generation.

original_entry.title: Exploring Audio Hallucination in Egocentric Video Understanding
original_entry.name: Audio Hallucination QA
original_entry.description: Probes imagined foreground and background sounds in egocentric videos through questions targeting visible but inaudible events.

records.protocol: Four dimensions and 15 subtasks; exact-match reasoning accuracy plus a separately reported multimodal-hallucination dimension.
records.rationale: The primary target is multi-hop long-form audio-visual reasoning. Its MH dimension is relevant, but the complete benchmark is not dedicated to hallucination.

original_entry.title: TraceAV-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-Hop Trajectory Reasoning over Long Audio-Visual Videos
original_entry.name: TraceAV-Bench
original_entry.description: Tests multi-hop reasoning and hallucination robustness using explicit evidence trajectories distributed across long audio-visual recordings.

records.protocol: AVHalluBench pairs videos with human audio/visual factual descriptions for hallucination scoring and model-ranking validation.
records.rationale: A separately named, dedicated audio-visual hallucination benchmark within the broader CrossCheckGPT paper.

original_entry.title: CrossCheckGPT: Universal Hallucination Ranking for Multimodal Foundation Models
original_entry.name: AVHalluBench
original_entry.description: Provides an audio-visual hallucination benchmark with human judgments for evaluating whether generated descriptions remain consistent with multimodal evidence.

records.protocol: Long-video reasoning answers plus temporal and semantic evidence scores; unmatched evidence is penalized.
records.rationale: The core objective is deep audio-visual reasoning and evidence grounding. Penalizing fabricated evidence does not make the overall benchmark a dedicated video-hallucination test.

original_entry.title: Video-HolmesV2: Can MLLMs Reason with Spatio-Temporal Audio-Visual Evidence in Long Videos?
original_entry.name: Video-HolmesV2
original_entry.description: Requires long-video answers to cite precise audio-visual evidence, using evidence-aware scoring to penalize guessing and fabricated support.

records.inspected_sections: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.1.2 and 3.3; Appendix A.1.4
records.protocol: Short/long-video emotion perception with basic/hallucinated QA pairs; paired accuracy and Yes-bias diagnostics.
records.rationale: Retain the dedicated video emotion-hallucination conditions. Text-only psychology, image-only, and audio-only tests are outside this video entry; emotion labels remain annotation-dependent.

original_entry.title: EmotionHallucer: Evaluating Emotion Hallucinations in Multimodal Large Language Models
original_entry.name: EmotionHallucer
original_entry.description: Evaluates emotion hallucinations in psychological knowledge and multimodal perception through adversarial questions about emotional cues and their interpretation.

2610.12458.summary: Benchmarks structured audio-visual captioning, separating hallucination-sensitive precision from omissions and diagnosing identity drift, temporal errors, and incorrect sound-to-shot associations.
2610.12458.evidence: Abstract; Introduction; Sections 3.2 and 4.1-4.3; Table 4; author project and resource pages

scope_review.reason: Broader audio-visual captioning benchmark with explicit prediction-to-reference precision penalizing hallucinated descriptions and dedicated sound-to-shot and speaker-attribution diagnostics.

2605.09904.summary: Tests object identity, state, and continuity with trajectory-grounded questions designed to require temporally ordered visual evidence.

scope_review.reason: Object-consistency benchmark includes hallucination-aware variants and Hallucination Diagnostic Accuracy, providing direct relevance within a wider evaluation.

2603.24329.summary: Uses synchronized multiplayer gameplay views and structured distractors to test agent identity, role attribution, and grounded reasoning.

scope_review.reason: Agent-centric video understanding benchmark explicitly diagnoses temporal, role, and fabricated-content errors through structured distractors.

2503.21459.summary: Provides diverse social-media road videos and question-answer pairs for evaluating road-event understanding across viewpoints and geographic settings.

scope_review.reason: Road-event VideoQA includes non-road videos and irrelevant/adversarial questions specifically testing hallucination robustness; the broad title does not justify exclusion.

2605.07593.summary: Tests multi-hop reasoning and hallucination robustness using explicit evidence trajectories distributed across long audio-visual recordings.

scope_review.reason: Long audio-visual reasoning benchmark explicitly includes a multimodal hallucination dimension alongside three broader reasoning dimensions.

2609.17248.summary: Requires long-video answers to cite precise audio-visual evidence, using evidence-aware scoring to penalize guessing and fabricated support.

scope_review.reason: Primarily long audio-visual reasoning, but evidence-conditioned scoring penalizes unsupported evidence. Its token-compression method is not separately listed as hallucination mitigation.
